author: Washington Irving
purpose: Resolve the first 30 reader-friction and named-reference holes from the opening source-gate sample, using the Anderson House search pattern, so only verified useful reader aids advance.
rule: PURPOSE -> STATE -> HOLE -> CAST -> COLLECT -> COMPARE -> FIT -> TEST -> VERIFY -> ASSEMBLE -> WAREHOUSE
done_criteria: Contextual function is stated without changing Irving's text.
Material factual/meaning claims use traceable evidence and independent-origin checking where needed.
Period fit and local-context fit are checked.
Contradictions or alternate senses are recorded rather than hidden.
Return is either VERIFIED_READER_AID, NO_MATERIAL_AID, or RECAST with the missing evidence named.
Every return preserves job_id and is eligible for marriage back to this batch.

jobs.local_context: The opening epigraph ends with “CASTLE OF INDOLENCE.”
jobs.question: Identify the quoted work/author and explain what the epigraph is doing here.

jobs.local_context: The story is presented as “FOUND AMONG THE PAPERS OF THE LATE DIEDRICH KNICKERBOCKER.”
jobs.question: Identify Knickerbocker and explain the framing function for Irving's tale.

jobs.local_context: Irving says Sleepy Hollow may have been bewitched by “a High German doctor.”
jobs.question: Determine the period meaning/reference of “High German” here and whether a reader note is useful.

jobs.local_context: Irving says the area was discovered by “Master Hendrick Hudson.”
jobs.question: Identify the historical referent and the function of this allusion in context.

jobs.local_context: The headless horseman is said to be a Hessian killed during the Revolutionary War.
jobs.question: Give only the minimum historical context needed to understand the claim in the story.

jobs.local_context: The rustic lads of the glen are called “the Sleepy Hollow Boys.”
jobs.question: Decide whether this is a local label created by the narration or a reference needing explanation.

jobs.local_context: Dutch navigators are said to implore the protection of St. Nicholas when crossing the Tappan Zee.
jobs.question: Identify the relevant St. Nicholas tradition and its narrative function without overexplaining.

jobs.local_context: Irving names the broad expansion of the Hudson as the Tappan Zee.
jobs.question: Identify the place and any period naming context material to a reader.

jobs.local_context: Irving says the nearby port is called Greensburgh by some.
jobs.question: Resolve the historical/geographic reference and spelling without silently correcting Irving.

jobs.local_context: Irving says the port is more generally known as Tarry Town.
jobs.question: Resolve the historical place name and the joke/folk etymology function in the passage.

jobs.local_context: Irving calls the river expansion “denominated by the ancient Dutch navigators the Tappan Zee.”
jobs.question: Resolve the period/contextual sense of “denominated.”

jobs.local_context: The housewives complain of their husbands' “inveterate propensity” to linger at the tavern.
jobs.question: Resolve “inveterate” in this phrase and test whether it creates real reader friction.

jobs.local_context: The narrator says he merely “advert[s] to it” for precision.
jobs.question: Resolve the period sense of “advert to” and whether a brief note is warranted.

jobs.local_context: A brook has enough murmur to “lull one to repose.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and decide whether the word needs support.

jobs.local_context: The quail and woodpecker barely break the “uniform tranquillity.”
jobs.question: Resolve the sense and reader-friction level.

jobs.local_context: The narrator recalls that “when a stripling” he went squirrel-shooting.
jobs.question: Resolve the period meaning and likely modern-reader friction.

jobs.local_context: The gunshot was “prolonged and reverberated by the angry echoes.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual function and decide if explanation adds value.

jobs.local_context: Sleepy Hollow is described as a “sequestered glen.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and reader-friction level.

jobs.local_context: Its lads are described as “rustic.”
jobs.question: Resolve the sense/register here and avoid importing a modern pejorative meaning unless supported.

jobs.local_context: A dreamy influence seems to “pervade the very atmosphere.”
jobs.question: Resolve the sense and reader-friction level.

jobs.local_context: Irving says an Indigenous chief “held his powwows there.”
jobs.question: Resolve the period usage, cultural reference, and any modern-reader/context issue without rewriting the source.

jobs.local_context: The inhabitants are said to walk in “a continual reverie.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and reader-friction level.

jobs.local_context: The inhabitants hold “marvellous beliefs.”
jobs.question: Resolve the period/contextual sense, including whether it means wonderful or supernatural/extraordinary here.

jobs.local_context: The inhabitants “are subject to trances and visions.”
jobs.question: Resolve the period/contextual sense without medicalizing the fictional passage.

jobs.local_context: The nightmare appears “with her whole ninefold.”
jobs.question: Determine what “ninefold” refers to here; this is a high-priority ambiguity and may require recast across literary/folklore sources.

jobs.local_context: The nightmare's ninefold makes the valley the favorite scene of her “gambols.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and tone.

jobs.local_context: The dominant spirit is “the apparition of a figure on horseback, without a head.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and whether support is useful.

jobs.local_context: The ghost is said to be a “Hessian trooper.”
jobs.question: Explain the historical referent at the minimum level needed to understand the story and verify period fit.

jobs.local_context: The narrator calls the headless horseman a “spectre.”
jobs.question: Resolve the contextual sense and period spelling/register.
